v.why: Filling an empty input-to-output edge with a convolution adds a path (experiments 6-10 positive), whereas replacing an existing skip connection removes a useful residual (experiments 1-5 all negative).
When edge 5 is empty, edge 3 may be the only route to the output, so making it a convolution reconnects the cell (experiment 6: +44.6 on CIFAR-10 versus small changes in 7-10).
Adding a skip from input to output where none exists gives the largest gains (experiments 81, 85) compared with replacing an existing operation on that edge.
Removing edge 3 when edge 5 is also empty leaves at most one path to the output, sometimes none (experiments 21, 23, 28, 29 are the worst drops).
If node 2 gets no direct input from node 0, upgrading its output edge helps little (experiments 11-12) compared with when edge 1 feeds node 2 (experiments 13-18: +11 to +49 on CIFAR-10).
Replacing average pooling on the last edge with an identity removes harmful smoothing just before the output (experiments 44, 48 strongly positive).
Replacing a 3x3 convolution on the last edge with a skip removes useful capacity (experiments 43, 47, 49 negative on all datasets).
Without a direct input-to-output edge, a convolution on edge 4 provides a key or the only path to the output (experiment 91: +49.5 on CIFAR-10; experiment 92 positive on all datasets).
Swapping a 3x3 convolution on the node1-to-node2 edge for pooling loses learned capacity (experiments 54, 58, 59 among the most negative).
If edge 3 already holds a strong convolution, turning it into a skip gains less than filling an empty or pooled edge (experiment 87 versus 85/88, experiment 83 versus 81).

raw:
Summary of what the 100 experiments show:

- **Edits that reconnect a broken cell help a lot.** When the input-to-output paths are cut (edge 3 = none, edge 1 = none, or edge 5 = none), adding an operation that reconnects them gains about 15–55 pp on CIFAR-10. The same edit in an already connected cell does much less (experiments 6, 13, 17, 85, 91).
- **Removing edge 3 hurts most when it is the only remaining route to the output.** This happens when edges 4 and 5 are already none (experiments 21 and 29, about −53 pp on CIFAR-10).
- **What the edit replaces matters.** Swapping a skip connection or a 3×3 convolution for something else usually hurts. Swapping out an average pool, especially on the output edges, usually helps.
